a_restatement: Memory is described as an architectural mechanism, not marketing—memory objects store values (text, image, or audio) and metadata including timestamp, what triggered its storage, and interaction summary.

When queried, the system scores stored memory objects for relevance by comparing query embeddings to memory value embeddings using cosine similarity, selects a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

The system manages the memory lifecycle: new matching input replaces or updates existing memories (or aligned objects merge), "forget that" commands delete immediately, time-specific deletion is queued (like "forget after three months"), and a maintenance cycle auto-deletes expired objects.

b_answers.answer: The model decides what is worth remembering from cached inputs and extracts it, and one trigger is when you explicitly ask the agent to remember something.
b_answers.quoted_span: A model decides what to store: cached inputs go to the model system, which predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it.

b_answers.answer: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object.

b_answers.answer: The agent scores memory objects by relevance to your query using cosine similarity of query embeddings and memory value embeddings, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
b_answers.quoted_span: the agent scores stored memory objects for relevance to your query. It compares a query embedding to memory value embeddings by a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

b_answers.answer: The "forget that" command deletes the specified information.
It is queued for deletion to occur after the specified time period.
b_answers.quoted_span: "forget this after three months" queues it for deletion

b_answers.answer: The old memory object is replaced or updated by the new matching input. If objects are aligned they can merge, and values are refined by contradicting input rather than overwritten.
b_answers.quoted_span: new timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated. Aligned objects can merge, and a value kept with supporting interactions is refined by contradicting input, not overwritten.

b_answers.answer: The problem is that agents forget and users must re-enter the same details repeatedly. This system is claimed to be different by being a described architecture using memory objects made from interactions (some on explicit request), retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when requested.
b_answers.quoted_span: When an AI agent says it "remembers" you, is that architecture or marketing? Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details; the claim is a loop — query plus memory data from a datastore of your past interactions, into a sequence model, out as a response.
